meta.schema: place_id refers to db/cities.json (line kinds use a list of place_ids); lat/lon null where no verified coordinate exists. Page = printed page (ghav printed = PDF-27, ghavi = PDF-27, ghavii = PDF-24).

gaps: Dirr: named (p.175) but no cities.json entry or verified coordinate.
Say (Sai Island) and Hannik: anchors kept with lat/lon null (Wikidata Q49677083 coordinate conflicts with the source; Hannik has no verified QID).
End of the Ottoman Habesh/Suakin administration and its 1865 transfer to Egypt: not found in the sources read; date_end left open.
Kassala founding / 1840s garrison: sources read give only 'conquest of al-Taka' in 1841.

Equatoria and Red Sea coast incorporation under Ismail: p.372 gives the reign only, no per-place dates beyond Gondokoro 1874, Lado 1876. GHA p.370 dates Baker 1869-73 yet has him arriving at Gondokoro in 1874 - VERIFY.
El Obeid's exact fall date (Jan 1883) not stated in sources read; only 'key towns of Kordofan' by Nov 1883.
Jabal Kadir (hijra 1881): no cities.json entry or verified coordinate.
Zubayr period end (arrest in Cairo, Sulayman's defeat): undated in p.371.

anchors.label_ar: أسوان: حامية بوسنية عثمانية [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Özdemir Pasha, who re-occupied Ibrim, Aswan and Say, garrisoning them with Bosnian troops
a garrison of Bosnian soldiers was installed at the fortresses of Aswan, Ibrïm and Say.

anchors.note: Date given only as "the middle of the century" (p.145); rear fortress of Ottoman Nubia (Berberistan).

anchors.label_ar: إبريم: قلعة حدودية عثمانية [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Özdemir Pasha, who re-occupied Ibrim, Aswan and Say, garrisoning them with Bosnian troops
Özdemir captured the strategic frontier fortresses of Ibrîm and Dirr. At Say, between the Second and Third Cataracts, he built a fortress which constituted the southern limit of Ottoman Egypt.

anchors.note: Ibrim and Dirr are named as frontier fortresses; Dirr (seat of the hereditary Kashif, p.175) has no cities.json entry and no coordinate taken.

anchors.label_en: Say (Sai Island): southern limit of Ottoman Egypt
anchors.label_ar: جزيرة صاي: الحد الجنوبي لمصر العثمانية [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Özdemir captured the strategic frontier fortresses of Ibrîm and Dirr. At Say, between the Second and Third Cataracts, he built a fortress which constituted the southern limit of Ottoman Egypt.
Özdemir Pasha, who re-occupied Ibrim, Aswan and Say, garrisoning them with Bosnian troops

anchors.note: NO COORDINATE: Wikidata Q49677083 (Sai Island) gives P625 18.75N 30.53E, which conflicts with the source ("between the Second and Third Cataracts"); not used. Map Designer: place only after a cited coordinate is added.

anchors.label_ar: حنّيك: الحدود العثمانية الفونجية المستقرة [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: The Egyptian frontier was finally consolidated at Hannîk after some fighting between the 'Abdalläbi and the Ottomans in about 1622. Hannîk lies half way between the Third Cataract and Mushu, the Fundj frontier post in the north.

anchors.note: NO COORDINATE: Hannik is not in cities.json and no Wikidata coordinate was verified; source places it half way between the Third Cataract and Mushu. Supersedes Say as the southern limit from c.1622.

anchors.date: mid-16th c. onward (end not stated in sources read)
anchors.label_ar: سواكن: حامية سنجق عثمانية [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Sawäkin, which was nominally dependent on Mamluk Egypt, passed to Ottoman suzerainty, and Massawa was annexed in 1557. Thenceforward the coastal strip between the two ports constituted the province of Habes. At Sawäkin, an Ottoman garrison, headed by a governor with the rank of sandjak was stationed.

anchors.note: Passed from nominal Mamluk dependence to Ottoman suzerainty under Özdemir.

anchors.label_ar: مصوع: ضمّها العثمانيون (مركز الحبش) [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: In 1557, Özdemir Pasha took Massäwa on the Red Sea coast

Sawäkin, which was nominally dependent on Mamluk Egypt, passed to Ottoman suzerainty, and Massawa was annexed in 1557. Thenceforward the coastal strip between the two ports constituted the province of Habes. At Sawäkin, an Ottoman garrison, headed by a governor with the rank of sandjak was stationed.

anchors.note: p.145: "Massäwa became the centre of Habesh, a new Ottoman province in Africa".

anchors.date: 1557 onward (end not stated in sources read)
anchors.label_ar: الحبش: الشريط الساحلي بين سواكن ومصوع [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Sawäkin, which was nominally dependent on Mamluk Egypt, passed to Ottoman suzerainty, and Massawa was annexed in 1557. Thenceforward the coastal strip between the two ports constituted the province of Habes. At Sawäkin, an Ottoman garrison, headed by a governor with the rank of sandjak was stationed.

anchors.note: Draw as a coastal strip between the two ports; inland depth is not stated, so keep it narrow and APPROXIMATE.

anchors.label_ar: سنار تستسلم (نهاية السلطنة الزرقاء) [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: their counterparts in Sennär capitulated to the Turkish rulers in 1821.
By the defeat of Sennär and Kordofan in that year the nucleus of what is now the Democratic Republic of the Sudan was founded.

anchors.note: Nucleus of Turco-Egyptian Sudan with Kordofan.

anchors.label_ar: فتح كردفان (الأبيض كنقطة مرجعية) [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: By the defeat of Sennär and Kordofan in that year the nucleus of what is now the Democratic Republic of the Sudan was founded.

anchors.note: Source names the province (Kordofan), not El Obeid; El Obeid is used only as a locator.

anchors.label_ar: فتح التاكا (كسلا كنقطة مرجعية) [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Turkish control of the northern and central Sudan was rounded off in 1841 by the conquest of al-Taka - the region of Khür al-Käsh and the Red Sea Hills.

anchors.note: Source dates the conquest of al-Taka (region of Khur al-Gash and the Red Sea Hills) to 1841 and does not name Kassala; Kassala is a locator only. The founding of Kassala itself is not in the sources read (gap).

anchors.label_ar: غندكرو: قاعدة بيكر في الاستوائية [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Immediately after his arrival at Gondokoro in 1874, Baker faced the open hostility of the Bari people

anchors.note: Source: Baker and Gordon "were unable to extend Turkish administration in Equatoria beyond a few scattered posts" (p.370) - draw posts, not a filled province. NB the source's "1874" for Baker at Gondokoro conflicts with its own Baker dates (1869-73, p.370) - flagged VERIFY in the gaps list.

anchors.label_ar: لادو: نقطة الانسحاب في الاستوائية [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: This forced Gordon in 1876 to order an immediate withdrawal northward to Lado.

anchors.note: Gordon withdrew northward from Buganda to Lado in 1876.

anchors.label_ar: بور: حامية حكومية محاصرة [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: the Jieng and Noath, under the leadership of a prophet called Donluly, besieged the government garrison at Bor.

anchors.note: Besieged by Jieng and Nuer (Noath) under Donluly; exact siege date not given.

anchors.label_en: Bahr al-Ghazal under al-Zubayr (Deim Zubeir as locator)
anchors.label_ar: بحر الغزال تحت الزبير (ديم الزبير كنقطة مرجعية) [يحتاج تحقق]
anchors.controlled_by: al-Zubayr Rahma Mansur (recognised governor under Khedive Ismail)

cites.quote: Khedive Ismail officially recognized Zubayr as the governor of Bahr al-Ghazäl.

anchors.note: Zubayr defeated a government expedition in 1872 and was then recognised as governor; the source does not name Deim Zubeir (locator only). p.371 adds the Turks "were unable to establish effective rule in Bahr al-Ghazäl".

anchors.label_ar: ضمّ دارفور بعد معركة منواشي [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: he was finally defeated and killed at the battle of Manwäshi in 1874, and Därfür was thus annexed to the Turkish regime.

anchors.note: Coordinate is Wikidata Q139553073 (a modern village named Manawashi); its identity with the 1874 battlefield is not confirmed by the source - VERIFY.

anchors.label_en: Northern limit at the Second Cataract (Wadi Halfa as locator)
anchors.label_ar: الحد الشمالي عند الشلال الثاني (وادي حلفا كنقطة مرجعية) [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: On the eve of the Mahdia the Sudan had thus formed an immense block of territory extending from the second cataract to the equatorial lakes and from the Red Sea to Därfür.

anchors.note: Overall extent on the eve of the Mahdiyya: second cataract to the equatorial lakes, Red Sea to Darfur. Wadi Halfa is a locator for the Second Cataract, not named in the source.

anchors.label_en: Shaykan: Hicks expedition destroyed; western Sudan lost
anchors.label_ar: شيكان: إبادة حملة هكس وسقوط الغرب [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Another turning-point in the history of the Mahdist revolution was the battle at Shaykän on 5 November 1883. By that time Khedive Tawfïk and his government were determined to crush the Mahdï, now in control of the key towns of Kordofân province.

the immediate consequence of the triumph at Shaykän was the total collapse of the Turco-Egyptian administration in the western Sudan and the establishment of Mahdist rule in the provinces of Kordofân, Därfür and Bahr al-Ghazäl.

anchors.note: Ends Turco-Egyptian rule in Kordofan, Darfur and Bahr al-Ghazal.

anchors.label_en: Kordofan towns in Mahdist hands (El Obeid)
anchors.label_ar: مدن كردفان بيد المهدية (الأبيض) [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Another turning-point in the history of the Mahdist revolution was the battle at Shaykän on 5 November 1883. By that time Khedive Tawfïk and his government were determined to crush the Mahdï, now in control of the key towns of Kordofân province.

anchors.note: Source says the Mahdi controlled "the key towns of Kordofân" by Nov 1883 but gives no date or name for El Obeid's fall - gap for an exact El Obeid date.

anchors.label_en: Suakin: only eastern port kept by the government
anchors.label_ar: سواكن: الميناء الشرقي الوحيد بيد الحكومة [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Except for Sawäkin, the Ansßr controlled the whole of the eastern Sudan

anchors.note: Everything else in the eastern Sudan was held by the Ansar under Uthman Digna.

anchors.label_en: Rejaf and Lado attacked; Bor garrison destroyed
anchors.label_ar: الرجاف ولادو تحت الهجوم وإبادة حامية بور [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: By 1885 the Bari chief Bego had exterminated this garrison and attacked Lado and Rejaf.

anchors.note: Local (Bari) resistance, not the Mahdist army.

anchors.label_en: Fall of Khartoum: end of Turco-Egyptian rule
anchors.label_ar: سقوط الخرطوم: نهاية الحكم التركي المصري [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: attacked the town, killed Gordon on 26 January 1885, and put an end to Turco-Egyptian rule in the Sudan.

anchors.note: End date for layer turco_egyptian (Suakin excepted).

anchors.label_ar: جزيرة أبا: أول انتصار للمهدية [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: the weak and disorganized expedition that was sent to deal with him in Aba Island. A brief skirmish followed in which the Ansßr achieved a quick and easy victory
a struggle which lasted for four years (1881-5)

anchors.note: Year from "four years (1881-5)"; exact day not given. The hijra to Jabal Kadir followed (no coordinate - gap).

anchors.label_en: Mahdist control of the Kordofan towns (El Obeid)
anchors.label_ar: سيطرة المهدية على مدن كردفان (الأبيض) [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Another turning-point in the history of the Mahdist revolution was the battle at Shaykän on 5 November 1883. By that time Khedive Tawfïk and his government were determined to crush the Mahdï, now in control of the key towns of Kordofân province.

anchors.note: Locator; source does not name El Obeid.

anchors.label_ar: انتصار شيكان [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Another turning-point in the history of the Mahdist revolution was the battle at Shaykän on 5 November 1883. By that time Khedive Tawfïk and his government were determined to crush the Mahdï, now in control of the key towns of Kordofân province.

anchors.note: Shaykan forest near al-Obeid.

anchors.label_en: Mahdist rule in Darfur and Bahr al-Ghazal (Deim Zubeir as locator)
anchors.label_ar: حكم المهدية في دارفور وبحر الغزال (ديم الزبير كنقطة مرجعية) [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: the immediate consequence of the triumph at Shaykän was the total collapse of the Turco-Egyptian administration in the western Sudan and the establishment of Mahdist rule in the provinces of Kordofân, Därfür and Bahr al-Ghazäl.
By 1883 the Jieng chiefs actively co-operated with the Mahdist forces to overthrow the Turkish regime in Bahr al-Ghazäl

anchors.note: Provinces named, no towns; draw Kordofan/Darfur/Bahr al-Ghazal from existing province shapes, hatched.

anchors.label_en: Eastern Sudan under Uthman Digna (Suakin excluded)
anchors.label_ar: شرق السودان تحت عثمان دقنة (عدا سواكن) [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: Except for Sawäkin, the Ansßr controlled the whole of the eastern Sudan

anchors.note: Suakin marks the EXCLUDED enclave; the Berber-Suakin route was cut.

anchors.label_ar: دخول المهدية الخرطوم [يحتاج تحقق]

cites.quote: attacked the town, killed Gordon on 26 January 1885, and put an end to Turco-Egyptian rule in the Sudan.

anchors.note: End of the 1881-85 advance.
